articles.title: I built an after-hours front desk that runs on the shop's own laptop, in the owner's voice, with no cloud AI
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle It is 7:04 PM in East Tennessee. The shop is dark, the trucks are I build software for small trade businesses ou…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle The call every small shop misses It is 7:04 PM in East Tennessee. The shop is dark, the trucks are parked, and the owner is at the kitchen table. The office phone rings four times and goes to voicemail. On the other end is a homeowner whose heat just quit, with a baby in the house, deciding which name on Google to try next. She does not leave a message. Almost nobody does. She calls the next shop. I build software for small trade businesses out here: HVAC companies, plumbers, excavators, tree crews. Most of them are one or two trucks. They cannot staff a phone at night, and the answering services they can afford sound like answering services.

articles.title: # How can I use my resume to prepare for the interview questions I’m most likely to face?
articles.excerpt: Many job seekers prepare for interviews by searching for common questions online and memorising sample answers. That can help, but there’s a more targeted approach: use your resume and the job descrip…
articles.body: Many job seekers prepare for interviews by searching for common questions online and memorising sample answers. That can help, but there’s a more targeted approach: use your resume and the job description together to build your interview preparation plan. Here’s how I would approach it. 1. Treat your resume as a list of potential interview topics Every achievement, project, responsibility, skill, and career transition on your resume could lead to a question. For example, if your resume says you improved a business process, be ready to explain: What problem were you trying to solve? What did you personally do? What challenges did you face? What was the outcome? What would you do differently today? Don't just prepare to repeat what's written on your resume.

articles.title: Building a zero-dependency poker fold-equity calculator in one HTML file
articles.excerpt: I wanted a bluff calculator that a poker player could open on a phone at the table, with nothing to install and no account to make. The result is one HTML file, vanilla JavaScript, no build step, serv…
articles.body: I wanted a bluff calculator that a poker player could open on a phone at the table, with nothing to install and no account to make. The result is one HTML file, vanilla JavaScript, no build step, served as static files on Netlify. Live version: https://madmanpoker.netlify.app (Full disclosure: I also write poker books, and the footer links to one.) The break-even formula Start with fold equity: the share of a bet's value that comes from opponents folding. For a pure bluff, where you have no outs and nothing to win when called, the bet breaks even when: alpha = bet / (pot + bet) Half a pot needs 33% folds. Two-thirds pot needs 40%. A pot-sized bet needs 50%. The calculator shows this number first, because it's the one players can compare against their own read of the opponent.

articles.title: Claude Code Agent Loop Deep Dive (5): The QueryEngine Main Loop as a State Machine
articles.excerpt: The first four posts explored individual mechanisms inside the loop: tool declarations, approval, hooks, parallel scheduling, stop-reason handling, and recovery. This post puts them together. The hear…
articles.body: The first four posts explored individual mechanisms inside the loop: tool declarations, approval, hooks, parallel scheduling, stop-reason handling, and recovery. This post puts them together. The heart of Claude Code is not the familiar five-line pseudo-loop. It is an explicit state machine . Before every model call, the loop decides which path it should take; after every call, it decides what the next path should be. Recovery, retries, automatic compaction, and a Stop-hook veto are all first-class branches in that machine. This is a tour of the actual main loop: what one iteration does, how transitions drive it, and why recovery is modelled as state rather than nested exception handling. First, correct a naming misconception src/QueryEngine.ts is a roughly 45 KB file.

articles.title: The Open-Source Supply Chain Vulnerability: Tracking Custom Git Submodules & Private Package Registries for Client Apps
articles.excerpt: Modern web agencies rarely build client applications entirely from scratch. They assemble tailored web apps from a modular blend of open-source libraries, internal boilerplates, private GitHub or GitL…
articles.body: Modern web agencies rarely build client applications entirely from scratch. They assemble tailored web apps from a modular blend of open-source libraries, internal boilerplates, private GitHub or GitLab repositories, proprietary npm packages, and private PHP Composer registries. This architecture speeds up delivery and cuts duplicated work. It also creates a blind spot: the agency’s private supply chain. Private dependencies, submodules, and registry tokens are often tied to the personal accounts of individual developers. When a developer leaves unexpectedly, a token expires, or a repository permission is set wrong, client update pipelines stop. Security patches don’t deploy, and automated builds fail.

articles.title: Stop relying on hope: why data contracts need CI enforcement
articles.excerpt: You ship the job. It passes CI. Your dbt tests show green. You push to production, grab a coffee, and feel like a competent engineer. Then, at 3:00 AM, the downstream dashboard team wakes up to a Page…
articles.body: You ship the job. It passes CI. Your dbt tests show green. You push to production, grab a coffee, and feel like a competent engineer. Then, at 3:00 AM, the downstream dashboard team wakes up to a PagerDuty alert because your service decided that user_id should now be a string instead of an integer. The schema registry was updated, but nobody read the Slack announcement, and your pipeline just broke three critical financial reporting models. This is the state of most data engineering teams today. We call it "coordination," but it’s really just a polite term for guessing what the other team did. Data contracts aren't just fancy YAML files; they are the only thing standing between you and a weekend of debugging JSON parsing errors.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.

articles.title: Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal
articles.excerpt: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander.
articles.body: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis. Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world. The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.
